The proof uses `hh1` in one place only: the call to `flattening_contDiffAt`, which needs it for `SimilarityProfile.inner_smoothAt` and `q_pos`. The other factors do not need it. `physicalHeat_contDiffAt` needs `1 < 1 + h`, which follows from `hh`. The square-root denominator needs only `hs`. Nothing in the statement mentions `hh1`.

The case h ≥ 1/2 holds because of the junk value. I checked the definitions in the sources:
- `SimilarityProfile.q h p = coordinateQ (2*h) (1 - p.1, p.2.2)`.
- `coordinateQ a p = if hp : 0 < a ∧ a < 1 ∧ 0 < p.1 then Classical.choose … else 1`.

When h ≥ 1/2 we have 2h ≥ 1, so the condition `2*h < 1` fails at every point, including h = 1/2. Then `q h` is the constant 1 and `X h p = p.2.1 / 1`. This map is smooth (`contDiffAt_snd.fst.div_const`, or simplify to `p.2.1`), and its value at p is positive by `hs`. So `flattening h f = fun p => f (Real.log (X h p))` is C² at p by the same argument `hf.comp p ((hX.log hXpos.ne').of_le …)`. The heat factor and the `.mul`/`.div` steps with the square root work without change.

So splitting on `h < 1/2` proves the theorem without `hh1`, and the statement stays true.
